verdict: Vertex AI SDK and API Standards (2026)
details:
Decision: All Vertex AI integrations must use the Google Gen AI SDK (@google/genai) with current enterprise patterns.
Rules:
- Use @google/genai (the unified Google Gen AI SDK), not deprecated @google-cloud/vertexai or @google-cloud/aiplatform for generative AI.
- Always use Vertex AI mode: new GoogleGenAI({ vertexai: true, project, location }) for enterprise deployments. Never use API-key mode in production.
- Use streaming (generateContentStream) as the default for user-facing responses. Non-streaming (generateContent) only for background batch processing.
- Context Caching: use ai.caches.create() with TTL for stable system prompts over 32k tokens. Cache IDs are ephemeral and region-scoped.
- Function Calling: declare tools via JSON Schema with strict typing. Use mode 'AUTO' for general, 'ANY' to force tool use, 'NONE' to disable.
- Structured Output: use responseSchema with Zod-compatible JSON Schema for deterministic parsing. Never regex-extract from free text when structured output is available.
- Safety Settings: always specify HarmBlockThreshold per category. Never rely on defaults in production.
- Model Selection: prefer gemini-2.5-flash for speed-sensitive paths, gemini-2.5-pro for reasoning-heavy paths. Pin model versions in production (e.g., gemini-2.5-flash-preview-05-20), never use '-latest' aliases.
- Error Handling: catch GoogleGenAIError specifically. Never swallow or silently retry generation errors.
- Token Management: use countTokens() before sending large contexts. Stay under model limits with explicit truncation strategies, not silent failures.
- Grounding: use Google Search grounding (tools: [{ googleSearch: {} }]) for real-time factual queries. Use Vertex AI Search (retrieval: { vertexAiSearch: { datastore } }) for private enterprise data.

Decision: All code must meet enterprise-grade TypeScript and Next.js quality.
Rules:
- TypeScript strict mode is mandatory. No 'any', no 'ts-ignore', no 'as unknown as X' escape hatches.
- Use explicit return types on all exported functions and API handlers.
- All environment variables must use requireEnv() from src/lib/env.ts. No process.env fallbacks with || for infrastructure variables.
- Error boundaries: every async API route must have try/catch with structured error responses (status code, error code, user-safe message).
- Next.js App Router: use server components by default. 'use client' only when browser APIs (useState, useEffect, event handlers) are required.
- API routes: use NextRequest/NextResponse types. Validate request bodies with Zod or explicit type guards.
- No barrel exports (index.ts re-exports) in hot paths. Direct file imports only.
- Database access: always use getDb() from src/lib/spanner-pool.ts. Never instantiate new Spanner().
- Mutations must use requireAuth(req) from src/lib/middleware/auth.ts.
- Imports: prefer named imports over default imports. Group by: node builtins, external packages, internal aliases (@/lib, @/app).
- No console.log in production code. Use structured logging with context (operation, entity ID, timing).
- Prefer const assertions and discriminated unions over enums.
- All dates must be timezone-aware. Use Intl.DateTimeFormat with explicit timeZone: 'America/Los_Angeles' for user-facing dates.

Decision: All frontend code must conform to the Obsidian Weissach design language.
Rules:
- Color System: use curated HSL palette. Primary surfaces use #050505 (Void). No generic CSS colors (red, blue, green). All accent colors must harmonize with the amber/rose tinting system.
- Glass Surfaces (Liquid Glass 2.0): bg-white/[0.025], backdrop-blur-[24px], backdrop-saturate-[180%], border border-white/[0.08], shadow-[inset_0_1px_0_rgba(255,255,255,0.05)].
- Typography: font-mono for micro-copy (10px, uppercase, tracking-widest). text-zinc-400 for assistant text, text-white for user text. Use Inter or system-ui for body, monospace for data labels.
- Motion: all layout transitions use Framer Motion spring physics (stiffness: 450, damping: 45, mass: 0.5). 60fps requirement for all animations, no CSS transition jank.
- Radius Hierarchy: rounded-[24px] for cards, rounded-[28px] for inputs/pills. Consistent across all components.
- Cards: every card must have specular top-edge lighting (inset shadow). Use milled border patterns (border-t white/[0.08], border-b black/50).
- Mobile-First: use 100dvh for mobile heights. Implement haptic feedback (navigator.vibrate(4)) on critical actions. Handle iOS keyboard with visualViewport shifting.
- Citations: inline jewel pills with brand favicons (Google S2 service, sz=64). No bracket citations [1]. Milled letter chip fallback if favicon fails.
- Semantic HTML: one h1 per page, proper heading hierarchy. All interactive elements need unique descriptive IDs.
- No Tailwind unless explicitly requested. Use vanilla CSS with CSS custom properties for theming.
- No placeholder content. Generate real assets with image generation tools.
- Loading States: use Neural Pulse (radial expansion) or Orbital Radar (circular pulse with opacity decay) for AI thinking states. Never use generic spinners.

Decision: All infrastructure code must follow GCP enterprise patterns.
Rules:
- Spanner: use getDb('dbname') singleton from src/lib/spanner-pool.ts. Never new Spanner().
- Spanner Types: always type callbacks (.map((row: any) => ...), .runTransactionAsync(async (tx: any) => ...)). Strict mode rejects implicit any.
- Spanner Timestamps: use Spanner.COMMIT_TIMESTAMP (static property). Never Spanner.commitTimestamp() (does not exist in ^8.6.0).
- Spanner KeySets: use keys: ids.map(id => [id]) for transaction.read() tuples. Never pass flat arrays.
- Cloud Run: design for cold starts. No global state that cannot survive process restart. Use in-memory caches with explicit TTL.
- Secret Manager: all secrets via gcloud secrets / --set-secrets in deploy scripts. Never hardcode in env or source.
- Retry Strategy: use exponential backoff with jitter for transient errors. Never use retries to mask deterministic bugs.
- Connection Pooling: respect gRPC channel limits. One Spanner pool per process via singleton pattern.
- Schema Changes: every DDL change requires a migration note and backwards-compatibility assessment. Never ALTER TABLE in production without a rollback plan.

Decision: All code output must meet security-first review standards.
Rules:
- No hardcoded secrets, API keys, or tokens in source code. All credentials via Secret Manager or requireEnv().
- Input Validation: validate and sanitize all user input at the API boundary. Use Zod schemas for structured validation.
- SQL Injection: use parameterized queries exclusively. Never concatenate user input into query strings.
- XSS: sanitize all user-generated content before DOM insertion. Use textContent over innerHTML.
- Auth: requireAuth(req) on every mutation endpoint. Read endpoints require auth unless explicitly public.
- CORS: explicit origin allowlists. Never use Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.
- Rate Limiting: implement per-user or per-IP rate limiting on expensive operations (AI generation, database writes).
- Error Messages: never leak stack traces, file paths, or internal IDs in user-facing error responses.
- Dependency Hygiene: pin exact versions in package.json for production dependencies. Use --legacy-peer-deps only when documented.
- PII: never log personally identifiable information (names, emails, SSNs, DOBs). Redact before structured logging.

Decision: This system operates under Git-governed rules. The AI's behavior is constitutionally bound to the ledger files in docs/ledger/.
Rules:
- Every code response must be consistent with the rules defined in this ledger.
- When a ledger rule conflicts with a user request, the ledger rule takes precedence unless the user explicitly overrides with justification.
- Code suggestions that violate ledger rules must include a warning explaining which rule is violated and why.
- The AI must never suggest patterns that contradict AGENTS.md hard rules.
- When uncertain about a pattern, cite the relevant ledger rule or AGENTS.md section.
- All architecture decisions must be traceable to a governance rule or an explicit user override.
